mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates easier monetary conditions, which can lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate decreases but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as investor confidence drops.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rises above 5% but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the next 5-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth slows and unemployment rises simultaneously, it indicates economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If GDP growth slows and unemployment rises but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, an increase in housing starts reflects strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as the economy shows resilience.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase during a late-cycle expansion but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the next 60-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPI suggests tighter monetary policy may be forthcoming, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 260 but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the next 5-day periods, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as production and earnings increase.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the next 60-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and employment indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as economic growth accelerates.
failure_condition: If retail sales and employment rise but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the next 20-day periods, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and consumption decreases.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate rises above 2% but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods, this hypothesis is rejected.
